Maya: Heads-up — onboarding Navis13b (quant int4) is hitting intermittent OOMs during long-context streaming (>6k tokens). Seen after ~30m of sustained traffic, fragmentation spikes then full OOMs.
Maya: Attach from last run:
```
[2026-03-20T15:12:08Z] ERROR OOM: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-20T15:12:08Z] heap: total=31.9G free=2.1G largest_free=850M
[2026-03-20T15:12:08Z] kv_cache: 12.4G used, prefetch=2.1G
[2026-03-20T15:12:08Z] evict: tried=3 freed=0
```
Maya: Notable: evictions didn't free enough, fragmentation looks like the culprit. Prefetch appears enabled by default for this model.
Oliver: Quick mitigation: disable prefetch for Navis13b on canary. Also lower model-level max_new_tokens default from 1024 -> 256 while we debug.
Oliver: Proposed runtime snippet to roll to 5% traffic:
```yaml
model_overrides:
  navis13b-int4:
    prefetch: false
    max_new_tokens_default: 256
    soft_reserve: 0.18  # conservative soft reserve to avoid slab exhaustion
    batch_window_ms: 8
```
Jamal: Agree. Also try KV eviction tweak: set `kv_eviction_trigger_ratio` to 0.65 and `kv_trim_granularity=64MB` to make evictions deterministic. Fragmentation suggests small free chunks. Increase slab alignment to 256KB for GPU allocator.
Jamal: Quick command for canary agent (will run):
```
redwoodctl models update navis13b-int4 --set prefetch=false --set max_new_tokens=256 --set kv_eviction_trigger_ratio=0.65
```
Maya: Heads-up on quality: some long-dialog prompts rely on 512+ new tokens. Lowering to 256 caused a small drop in our convo-completion eval (delta -1.7% F1 on testset). We should A/B route only low-risk traffic and run the eval suite.
Maya: I'll push a prompt-level override for evaluation flows so they keep 512 while general default is 256.
devex-bot: Evals queued: https://internal.redwood/evals/rounds/2026-03-20/navis13b-canary (includes conv-completion and qa-long tests).
Oliver: If canary looks fine, we'll keep prefetch disabled and leave soft_reserve=0.18 for 24h, then try progressive prefetch backoff instead of full disable: prefetch_backoff=linear(0.1->1.0) based on mem pressure.
Jamal: I'll run a heap-defrag stress job (30m sustained 8k context) on canary nodes with `slab_alignment=256KB` and `kv_trim_granularity=64MB` and report memory map. ETA 2h.
Maya: Assignments: Jamal -> infra tweaks + stress job. Oliver -> canary rollout (5%) and rollout rollback play. Maya -> evals and prompt overrides. I'll post results here. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy job 83421 started: rolling canary update navis13b-int4 -> prefetch=false, max_new_tokens=256 (5% traffic).
Oliver: Thanks. If we still see fragmentation after alignment/trim, next step is to try a different allocator plugin (jemalloc-slab) and re-run quantization export with padding-aligned tensors.
Maya: Noted. Keeping thread open for results.
